name: Club La Santa
who: Self-contained multisport campus on Lanzarote's lava coast, with stays from a few days to several weeks and full swim/bike/run infrastructure.
why: The original multisport training mecca, running since 1979 and the home base of IRONMAN Lanzarote.
takeaway: Book it as a training block, not a holiday — bring a plan for the swim, bike, run.

name: Playitas Resort
who: All-inclusive sports resort built around a multisport complex; week-long triathlon, athletics, and team-sport camps for pros and amateurs.
why: Voted among Europe's top triathlon training centres by pro athletes and coaches; hosts national federations year-round.
takeaway: Book a week-long triathlon or team-sport training camp here — pros and amateurs both train, not lounge.

name: Surf Simply
who: All-inclusive boutique surf-coaching resort; week-long stays built entirely around technical, video-analyzed surf instruction, from about $4,000/week.
why: Pioneered systemized surf coaching and is the most media-covered dedicated surf-coaching resort (NYT, Conde Nast, WSJ, CNN).
takeaway: Go to get coached on your surfing with video analysis — a technical surf school, not a surf-and-relax trip.

name: Thanyapura Sports Resort
who: Multisport campus resort with an Olympic-standard pool, athletics track, and structured triathlon/running programs; stays from days to months.
why: One of Asia's most established sport-science-backed training resorts, popular with pro triathletes overwintering in Thailand.
takeaway: Book this for structured triathlon or running training on Olympic-standard facilities — training camp, not a leisure resort.

name: HATC Iten
who: Lornah Kiplagat's high-altitude running base at 2,400m, with a gym, 400m track, and 25m pool; open bookings for recreational-to-elite runners, capped at 35 guests.
why: Founded by a five-time world champion; the best-known gateway into Kenya's Rift Valley running culture.
reach: IG ~1.1K (verified 2026-08, official account; most guest volume comes through partner tour operators)
takeaway: Book this to train at altitude on a legendary running base — any level runner, not a sightseeing trip.

name: Tiger Muay Thai
who: The world's largest Muay Thai/MMA/fitness training camp and destination gym, with on-site and partner accommodation from drop-in days to month-long stays.
why: The best-known combat-sports training destination worldwide, reporting around $20M in annual revenue and a huge expat fighter following.
takeaway: Go if you want to train like a fighter — 150+ weekly classes suit committed combat-sports travelers, not casual gym-goers.

name: Fairtex Training Center Pattaya
who: Legacy Muay Thai/MMA/BJJ camp with on-site dorms to private rooms; day drop-ins to monthly all-inclusive packages, open six days a week since 1971.
why: One of the sport's oldest and most fighter-decorated camps, having produced multiple Muay Thai champions under the Fairtex name.
takeaway: Go here to train like a champion at a decades-old fight camp — for fighters, not for a scenic getaway.

name: Viva Blue & Spa (Playa de Muro)
who: 4-star beach hotel that hosts week-long, coach-run triathlon training camps (25m pool, gym, quiet cycling roads) from about GBP 900/person.
why: One of Mallorca's most established third-party triathlon-camp venues, booked season after season by UK training operators.
reach: IG ~5K (approx 2026, hotel account; camp audience is carried mainly by tour operators)
takeaway: Book this through a triathlon tour operator for a coach-run training week — camp first, beach hotel second.

name: Zafiro Palace Alcudia
who: 5-star cycling-dedicated hotel with 350-bike storage, workshop, rental fleet, and organized routes; multi-night stays for clubs and individuals.
why: Mallorca's benchmark cycling hotel and an official IRONMAN Mallorca sponsor, drawing cycling clubs from across Europe each spring.
takeaway: Book this as a cycling-focused hotel with bike storage and organized routes — for clubs and cyclists, not general travelers.

name: Eat Sleep Cycle
who: Cycling tour operator and bike hub running multi-day packaged camps (bike, hotel, guided rides) out of pro-cyclist territory near Girona.
why: The best-known cycling-travel brand built around Girona's status as a pro-cyclist training hub.
takeaway: Book a packaged cycling camp with guided rides in pro-cyclist territory — for riders, not general sightseers.

name: Soul & Surf
who: Boutique surf, yoga, and massage retreats across three countries; all-inclusive week-long stays from about GBP 156/night.
why: A long-running, design-forward surf-retreat brand with a loyal following and a strong European client base.
takeaway: Book a week of surf, yoga and massage across its multi-country locations — relaxed surf-retreat, not intensive training.

name: RunningInKenya.com Kaptagat Camp
who: All-inclusive weekly running camps at 2,400m in Kaptagat — shared rooms, full board, structured altitude sessions plus optional safari add-ons.
why: Kaptagat is the training base of the NN Running Team and multiple world-record marathoners; these camps put recreational runners on the same roads.
takeaway: Book a week of structured altitude running on the roads elite marathoners train — for runners, safari is optional.

name: IMG Academy
who: Multi-sport athletic campus running adult and family performance camps across 11 sports nearly every week of the year, with discounted stays at the on-site Legacy Hotel.
why: The most recognized sports-performance brand in the US, built on decades of producing pro and Olympic athletes.
takeaway: Book a performance camp in one of 11 sports, not a leisure stay — the hotel is a bonus.

name: Vuokatti Sport
who: Olympic training-center resort with a ski tunnel, biathlon range, and roller-ski tracks; hotel/apartment stays from about EUR 95/night full board.
why: Scandinavia's benchmark winter-sport training base, used by World Cup ski and biathlon teams and open to public training camps.
takeaway: Book this for Olympic-grade ski and biathlon training facilities — winter-sport camp, not a general ski holiday.

name: Kandui Villas
who: Luxury surf resort and boat-accessible villas in the Mentawais, with optional paid surf coaching, video analysis, and theory sessions.
why: One of the most recognized names in Mentawai surf travel, sitting on some of Indonesia's most consistent reef breaks.
takeaway: Book this for optional paid surf coaching and video analysis on world-class reef breaks — surf-focused, coaching is extra.

name: Centro de Alto Rendimiento Sierra Nevada
who: Spain's national high-altitude training center at 2,320m, with a 50m pool and indoor/outdoor tracks; individuals and clubs book stays through specialist camp operators.
why: The reference altitude base for Spanish and visiting international athletics, cycling, and swimming squads for decades.
takeaway: Book this through a specialist camp operator for serious altitude training — an athlete's base, not a tourist stop.

name: Berghotel Turlwand
who: Family-run mountain hotel at 1,750m in Austria's Nordic-ski showcase region, booking single athletes or whole training camps against 220km of groomed trails and a biathlon range.
why: The lodging anchor of Ramsau's international Nordic training center, used by cross-country and biathlon national teams and open to individual bookings.
takeaway: Book this as a Nordic-ski or biathlon training base with 220km of groomed trails — for athletes, not casual skiers.

name: Crowie's Kona Training Camp
who: Multi-day triathlon training camp hosted at the Mauna Lani resort by three-time IRONMAN world champion Craig 'Crowie' Alexander, run on the Kona race course itself.
why: Led by a Kona legend on the actual world-championship course, the highest-prestige short-stay triathlon camp tied to a single race.
takeaway: Book this to train the actual Kona race course with a world-champion coach — a short, focused triathlon camp.
